Settings row

One setting as a row: its label and a one-line description, with a single control or a status at the far end.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • For a page of settings that each take effect by themselves: a switch, a choice from a short list, an account to connect.
  • For a group of related settings under one heading, such as Notifications or Connected accounts.
  • For a destructive setting, such as deleting a workspace, in a group of its own at the end of the page.

When not to use it

  • For values sent together with one button. Use fields in a form.
  • For a setting that needs more than one control or more than a line of explanation. Give it a view or a sheet of its own, and make the row's control a button that opens it.
  • For facts the reader cannot change. Use the key-value list.
  • For a list of things the reader opens. Use the list.

Variants

switch
The row holds one gw-switch and nothing else. The switch brings its own label, description, state in words and error.
select
gw-settings-row__text, then gw-settings-row__control holding a gw-select. The label is a label element for the select.
button
gw-settings-row__control holds one gw-button whose words name the action and the thing, such as Connect GitHub. Never primary.
status
gw-settings-row__control holds a p with gw-settings-row__status that says the state in words, such as Signed in as mira@acme.dev.
danger gw-settings-row--danger
A setting that deletes or cannot be undone. The label gets a warning mark, the description names what is lost and the control is a gw-button gw-button--danger that opens a confirm dialog.

Accessibility

  • A group is a div with gw-settings-row__group, role="group" and aria-labelledby pointing at its gw-settings-row__heading, a heading at the level the page needs. Each row is a div with gw-settings-row.
  • A row has one control. For a switch, put the gw-switch markup in the row by itself: its label and description stand in for gw-settings-row__text.
  • For a select, gw-settings-row__label is a label element whose for attribute is the select's id, and the select points at gw-settings-row__description with aria-describedby. The select saves on its change event, so the row needs no Save button.
  • For a button or a status, gw-settings-row__label is a p. The button's own words say what it does and to what, so it reads correctly out of context, and it points at the description with aria-describedby.
  • The description is one line that says what the setting does or what state it is in. A status, such as Connected or Not connected, is written in words.
  • When a control is unavailable, set the disabled attribute and say why in the description.
  • While a button's action runs, set aria-busy="true" on it and change its words to say what is happening, such as Connecting to GitHub.
  • If a change is not saved, put the control back to the saved value and add a p with gw-settings-row__error and role="alert" as the row's last child. It says what the setting still is and what to do, and its icon is drawn by the stylesheet.
  • A danger row's label is marked with an icon as well as the danger button's colour. Its button never deletes at once: it opens a confirm dialog that names the thing.
  • Below 768px the control sits under the text; from 768px it is at the far end of the row, centred on the text. Tab moves through the controls in order. The component needs no script.
